newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 22.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - April 22.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

The New South Wales state government would announce the A$1 billion public float of the horse racing betting agency, the Totalisator Agency Board (TAB), later on Tuesday, The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper said. A government spokesman said an announcement about TAB would be made early on Tuesday afternoon. AWA Ltd, Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd and Tabcorp Holdings Ltd were all seen as likely bidders in a trade sale if a float was not chosen.

Metromedia International Group Inc is in talks with Metro Goldwyn Mayer Inc and its primary backer, billionaire investor Kirk Kerkorian, regarding the sale of Metromedia's film library to MGM. Sources familiar with the talks said they believe MGM and Kerkorian have made a preliminary bid just above $300 million for Metromedia's 2,200-title catalog.
Amcor Ltd managing director Don Macfarlane said in a newspaper interview that the paper and packaging group planned to spend about A$200 million on acquisitions in the United States and Europe.
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$17.12 (-0.04)

A strike by 350 workers at Chile's giant Escondida mine has slowed down operations slightly but output of both concentrates and cathodes is normal, the mine's CEO Ken Pickering said. Pickering, speaking through a spokeswoman, said the mine was operating at 85 percent of normal levels and that the mine was redistributing work crews to ease the effects of the three-day-old walkout.
St Barbara Mines Ltd director Ross Atkins said in a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange on Tuesday that St Barbara's chief executive Robin Dean resigned as chief executive on April 3.
